lemmas.title: Hamming [7,4,3] code: 16 binary words of length 7 with minimum distance 3 (A(7,3) ≥ 16)
lemmas.paper_notes: List the 16 codewords of the [7,4,3] Hamming code as `BitVec 7` literals and close with `Codes.isBinaryCode_of_checkDist (by decide) (by decide +kernel)` plus `by decide` for the length (well under 1s).

lemmas.title: Hamming sphere-packing bound: every distance-3 binary code of length n has |C|·(n+1) ≤ 2^n
lemmas.paper_notes: Radius-1 balls around distinct codewords are disjoint (triangle inequality for hammingDist) and each holds n+1 words of BitVec n. Count the union inside the 2^n-word space; Core's popCountAux_add/popCountAux_mod lemmas help with bit bookkeeping. Together with EC-001 this gives A(7,3) = 16 exactly.

lemmas.title: Plotkin bound: if 2d > n then every binary code of length n and minimum distance d has |C|·(2d−n) ≤ 2d
lemmas.paper_notes: Double-count S = Σ_{pairs} hammingDist: S ≥ C(M,2)·d, and per coordinate a column with k ones contributes k(M−k) ≤ M²/4, so 2(M−1)d ≤ nM. Needs a per-coordinate decomposition of hammingWeight (popCountAux_add splits off one bit at a time).

lemmas.title: King of the Hill: Binary Code A(17,6) (World Record = 258, Upper Bound = 340)
lemmas.registered_statement: Codes.Statements.EC_rec_17_6.Record score  --  ∃ C : List (BitVec 17), score ≤ C.length ∧ IsBinaryCode 17 6 C
lemmas.paper_notes: Auto-ratcheting King-of-the-Hill hunt! Launch floor = 256 (Nordstrom–Robinson (16,256,6) code padded with a zero coordinate, from the extended Golay code). Literature record = 258 (Milshtein 2019, equivalently a (16,258,5) code); upper bound = 340 (Best–Brouwer–MacWilliams–Odlyzko–Sloane 1978, still the entry in Brouwer's table). The Core `checkDist` certificate (12-bit popcount table + Nat.rec loop, proved sound) checks all 32,640 pairs of the 256-word witness in ~1.6s in Lean 4.36 via `decide +kernel`; 340 words would take about 3s. Prove `¬ Record b` to lower the upper bound!

lemmas.title: King of the Hill: Constant-Weight Code A(17,6,7) (World Record = 166, Upper Bound = 206)
lemmas.registered_statement: Codes.Statements.EC_rec_17_6_7.Record score  --  ∃ C : List (BitVec 17), score ≤ C.length ∧ IsConstantWeightCode 17 6 7 C
lemmas.paper_notes: Auto-ratcheting King-of-the-Hill hunt! Launch floor = literature record = 166 (Golay-derived code, Brouwer–Shearer–Sloane–Smith 1990; explicit code in Brouwer's table at cwc/d6/a17.6.7.166). Upper bound = 206 (Polak 2017, SDP). `Codes.isConstantWeightCode_of_check (by decide) (by decide +kernel) (by decide +kernel)` verifies the 166-word witness in ~0.75s in Lean 4.36. A 167-word code is a new world record!

lemmas.title: King of the Hill: Constant-Weight Code A(20,8,10) (World Record = 176, Upper Bound = 206)
lemmas.registered_statement: Codes.Statements.EC_rec_20_8_10.Record score  --  ∃ C : List (BitVec 20), score ≤ C.length ∧ IsConstantWeightCode 20 8 10 C
lemmas.paper_notes: Auto-ratcheting King-of-the-Hill hunt! Launch floor = literature record = 176 (code with a prescribed automorphism group: two orbits of size 96 + 80, BSSS 1990; Brouwer's table at cwc/d8/i20.10). Upper bound = 206 (Agrell–Vardy–Zeger 2000). The 176-word witness verifies in ~0.8s in Lean 4.36 via the Core certificate checker. Try orbit unions under other permutation groups for 177+!
